idiom_name: single-pass loop carrying the seed and the accumulator (no stdlib machinery)
implementation_notes: C has neither generic recursion combinators nor lazy iterators, so the hylomorphism is written out literally: one loop that computes the next seed (the coalgebra) and immediately folds it into the accumulator (the algebra), so no array or tree is ever allocated. Keeping the two steps as separate functions - a state struct plus callbacks such as State (*next)(State) / long (*combine)(long, State) - preserves the pattern's separation and lets either half be swapped or unit-tested, and the driver stays a five-line loop. The materialized form is still the right choice when the same generated structure must feed several folds or must outlive one pass, because C offers no lazy re-iteration to rebuild it cheaply.
pitfalls: Fold direction and associativity: a left-fold loop over a non-associative algebra returns a different value than the right-fold version the functional formulation implies - decide the direction deliberately.
State structs passed by value copy on every step; pass a const pointer once the seed is large enough to matter.
Without generic machinery the driver is duplicated per shape, and a hand-rolled loop that caches an array for convenience silently reintroduces the intermediate structure.
